engagement_title: DAYDRIFT season four handover: pull a representative picture out of three episodes shot months apart and bring them to one channel look, recover the show name off the microphone flag, and rebuild the printer's episode card into a live nine record run
vertical: Music, film, publishing and media, independent long form interview podcast with a membership and one renewing sponsor (Portland, Oregon)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com YouTube podcast post carried in the ledger, where a two person show hands over raw episode recordings and asks for episodes shaped into something watchable, for light hearted graphics that match a casual fun vibe, for the client's existing logo carried across the channel branding, and for any custom graphic assets created to be delivered separately in transparent PNG or vector form. Two literal asks in that post are not connector work and are re cast honestly rather than faked. A timeline trim of pauses and stumbles has no connector analogue, because the shortening tool works from engagement rather than from timestamps, so the short vertical pieces are produced by that route and the brief asks for short cuts rather than for a re edited episode. Motion graphics composited over the picture are also unavailable, so the caption plate and the end card are delivered as editable canvases the show drops into its own editor, and the brief asks for a plate rather than for burned in captions. Everything else in that post is now genuinely producible: CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) confirms an ink level recovery off photographed printed collateral, a merge template reverse engineered out of a flat press PDF, and a native editable Express document carrying mixed canvas sizes, which is exactly the separately delivered, client editable asset set the poster asked for and never got.
client_one_liner: Season four is recorded and edited, our channel page looks like nine different shows, and the only place our name still exists as artwork is the foam flag on the microphone.
client_brief:
DAYDRIFT, season four handover

We are a two person interview show out of Portland. Nine episodes a season, one guest, long form, recorded in our own room. A few thousand regular listeners, about two hundred paying members at eight dollars a month, and one sponsor who renews if the numbers hold.

Here is where we are. Season four is recorded and the audio is edited. What we have never had is a look. Every episode goes up with whatever still we grabbed that week, so our page reads as nine different shows stacked on top of each other. We want one look all of them can sit inside, and we want it built so we can keep using it ourselves next season without coming back to you.

The recordings. Three of the nine are the ones to work from first. They were shot months apart and the room was honestly not the same each time. Please pull a picture out of each that actually represents that conversation, and bring the three of them to one look. Warm and lived in, like a room people talk in. Not a news set.

Short vertical pieces. One short vertical cut per episode for the feeds, and the speech needs to be cleaner than it is. Nothing stretched or blown up to fit. We would rather it be smaller and sharp.

The name. Our show name only exists as artwork on the foam flag on our microphone. The friend who drew it moved away and there is no file. We need it back as something we can put on anything, at any size, on dark or on light.

The cards. We print an episode card for the merch table at live tapings and mail one to every member. Last year's card came back from our printer as a print file and we still have it. Build this season's nine cards from that same card, each with its own episode details.

Also the thumbnails, a caption plate for the verticals and an end card, all in one working file we can open and change ourselves, because guests move and dates move.

Our listeners are thirty to fifty and most of them listen at work. And a written note on what you did and how to use the name.
price_band_and_audience: Independent long form podcast, eight dollar monthly membership, one modest renewing sponsor, listeners thirty to fifty. The band is load bearing. At this level the look has to read considered and hand made: warm domestic light, real texture in the room, restrained type, the picture of two people talking rather than a set. Push it toward broadcast, with a hard lit black seamless, a hard geometric grid and a network style lockup, and it misrepresents a two person show to the exact membership that pays for it because it is not that. Push it the other way into a scrappy meme treatment, with heavy outlines, arrows and shouted type, and it reads as the wrong genre entirely for a fifty minute interview and the sponsor renewal argument collapses. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent long form interview podcast with a YouTube channel, one guest per episode, made and recorded in the show's own room.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Started 2021 in Portland, Oregon. A two person show: two hosts, one room, nine episodes a season.
brand_identity.about: DAYDRIFT is a slow, unhurried interview show built around one guest and one real conversation that runs the better part of an hour. It is made by two people in a room they know well, funded by a small paying membership and one renewing sponsor. The promise is intimacy: you are sitting in on a talk between people who like each other, not watching a broadcast.
brand_identity.audience: Regular listeners aged thirty to fifty, most of them listening at work through the day. About two hundred paying members at eight dollars a month, plus a few thousand free listeners who click through to the channel page.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Membership at eight dollars a month with one modest renewing sponsor. Squarely independent: above hobby, well below a network production. The look must read considered and hand made, never broadcast and never scrappy meme.
brand_identity.typography: A warm humanist serif for the show name and episode titles, paired with a quiet humanist sans for credits, dates and body. Generous spacing, restrained weights, nothing condensed or shouted. Type should feel like a good paperback, not a title card.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, warm and a little understated, the way two friends actually talk. We never oversell a guest. Example line the brand would write: "Episode eight. We sat down with her for an hour and did not want it to end."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no brand files left. The show name only survives as artwork on the foam flag on the microphone, drawn years ago by a friend who has since moved away and left no source file. Last season's printed episode card exists only as the print file the printer returned. Everything else has to be rebuilt from those.
brand_identity.values: Honesty and warmth over polish. The show would rather be small and real than slick, and it wants a look it can keep running itself next season without re commissioning.

assets_supplied.name: daydrift_episodes/ (three episode recordings, season four)
assets_supplied.kind: Long form interview recordings, one guest each, fifty two to seventy four minutes, recorded months apart in the show's own room.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Episodes two, five and eight. Same room, same two chairs, same microphones."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The room was not the same each time. Episode five was recorded after a window was uncovered and carries a cold cast down the guest side only, while episode eight has a warm practical lamp burning behind the host. Episode two also came out of an older export at a smaller frame size than the other two, which no filename, folder or note reveals, so the vertical cut taken from it is bounded lower than its neighbours before any decision is made.

assets_supplied.name: daydrift_mic_flag.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the show's foam microphone flag standing on the desk, the wordmark printed in one deep ink across the soft foam face.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our name still exists as artwork."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The wordmark is disjoint lettering on a soft compressible surface, so the one call knockout keeps two or three letters, drops the rest and still returns success. The ink has spread into the foam, so the strokes are heavier and the counters tighter than the drawing ever was, which is invisible at full canvas and decisive at reproduction size. The flag's own colour also runs close to the wall behind it down the shadowed side of the frame.

assets_supplied.name: daydrift_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's episode card exactly as it went to the printer: single sided A6, episode number, title, guest credit, recording date, sponsor line and one picture window.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer made for us last year. We still have the print file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What that card becomes when it is opened as an editable document is nothing like what the printed page suggests. Its face can collapse into one continuous text frame carrying every line, with no separately addressable picture frame at all. The readout that lists that frame's text also drops one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short, and both the validator and the template preparation report success on the wrong offsets.

assets_supplied.name: daydrift_season4.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The season roster: nine episodes with number, title, guest, recording date, runtime, sponsor line and a per record picture column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every episode this season, exactly as we list them on the site."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One guest appears twice under two different spellings, and one episode title runs long enough that a fixed measure stops rendering it rather than pushing it, so the record reads complete in the data and arrives cut short at trim. The picture column also names nine pictures when only three episodes have been asked for as frames, which no column heading admits.

assets_supplied.name: daydrift_shownotes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the nine episode titles, the one line guest credits, the recording dates and the sponsor read line that is contractually required to appear on the card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Titles and credits as we publish them. The sponsor line is not ours to shorten."

acceptance_bar: The three episode pictures read as one channel when they are stacked the way a channel page stacks them: one white point, one black point, one warmth, one sense of how much room is in the frame. A picture that cannot be brought to the set is named, not shipped at eighty percent.

No delivered still, card picture or vertical cut exceeds the pixel dimensions of the recording or frame it came from, and no returned resize report carries an enlargement entry. Reaching a size by interpolation fails even where it looks acceptable.
Each of the three pictures represents its own episode, not the same three seconds of two people sitting still. The guest is recognisable and present in each.

The show name comes back as placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, every letter present, and it still reads as our name where it actually reproduces, on the dark band and reversed on light.
The nine cards are one press file with one record per page, page count equal to row count, every field on every card filled from its own row, and the sponsor line present and complete on all nine.
Every card is legible and complete at trim. A record whose title stops part way through is a failed card even when the merge reported success.
Where a card cannot carry what the roster promises, the gap is named in writing with what was delivered instead. Six episodes have no picture and nobody has said so yet.
The vertical cuts are shorter than their sources, carry cleaned speech, and are reframed by reduction only. Cleaning after cutting is not the same job and does not count.

All the channel canvases arrive in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, with the words as text we can retype, the name as real vector shapes and every picture carried inside the file rather than pointed at. The self contained source it was built from comes with it.
The caption plate still reads as a caption plate after it has been handed over, on every canvas and not only the first one.
One type system across every canvas and the note names, per role, the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.

The note states per picture what was applied and why that episode differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, the roster reconciliation, and what we can and cannot do with the recovered name.

adobe_surfaces.role: The front and the back of the engagement. It reads what each recording actually is before anything is planned, because the roster's episode numbers say nothing about a file's frame size and the vertical delivery height is bounded by the source. It pulls the representative picture out of each of the three episodes, cleans the speech before anything is cut so the cleaning applies to the whole take rather than to three chosen fragments, produces the short vertical pieces by the engagement route rather than by timestamps, and reframes to vertical by reduction only.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It fixes one channel target off the best lit of the three pulled pictures and corrects the other two toward it one call at a time rather than batching one parameter set across three different rooms, confines corrections where a whole frame move would take the guest's skin with the window, cuts the card pictures and the thumbnail pictures without enlarging anything, and recovers the wordmark at ink level off a photographed foam flag with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as mapper and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The nine episode cards, built out of the printer's own file so the season matches last season on the merch table. The template is reverse engineered from a flat press PDF, which means the frame inventory has to be read out of the round tripped document rather than assumed from the printed page, the true story text has to be reconstructed before a single offset is computed, and the placeholders have to be re verified after preparation because the preparation step reports success either way. Delivery is one press file with one record per page plus per record proofs, and the fact that bleed cannot be introduced into a PDF derived template is disclosed rather than faked.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The thumbnails, the vertical caption plate and the end card as one native editable document carrying roots at three canvas sizes, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout and the only one that leaves the show something it can change itself next season. Every picture must be pulled down and carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the recovered name goes in as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload travels as an uploaded file because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system carried across every canvas and recorded in the handover. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land warm and domestic rather than broadcast. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be read off a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by a weight, every name has to be laundered into canonical form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS has to use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cards are a record per page run and belong on the merge surface; the thumbnails, plate and end card are one off canvases the client must edit next season and only one surface here composes free form layout. The brief pins both destinations, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role, so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which episode.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Read what each of the three recordings actually is: frame size, duration and audio state, before any framing or delivery size is promised.
trajectory.judgement: The roster asserts three episodes of one show. Episode numbering is not evidence about a file, and the vertical delivery height is bounded by whatever the smallest source turns out to be.
trajectory.produces: A per recording note of true dimensions, duration and audio condition.

trajectory.action: Pull a representative picture out of each of the three episodes.
trajectory.judgement: Representative means the conversation, not the prettiest hundredth of a second. A frame where the guest is mid sentence and present beats a frame where both people happen to be still.
trajectory.produces: Three candidate pictures, one per episode, at each recording's own scale.

trajectory.action: Preview all three pulled pictures and triage them: where each frame's neutral actually sits, which side of the frame the light is coming from, what is off level, and how much room each has around the two people.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes it is the same room three times. The pictures are the only place that can be settled, and a cold window on one side of one frame is a different correction from a warm lamp behind the host.
trajectory.produces: A per picture triage note covering illuminant, tilt, and available room around the subjects.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop that has already been committed.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one channel target off the best lit picture and correct the other two toward it with their own calls, recording the parameters applied to each.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set of three, not three good pictures. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for three different rooms. The destination is held constant and reached by different routes.
trajectory.produces: Three graded masters at source scale with a per picture parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confine corrections where a whole frame move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the substrate pulls the selection to the wall. Pulling the cold window side of one frame back without taking the guest's skin with it is a confined move, not a global one.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole frame move would have taken the skin green or the room muddy.

trajectory.action: Recover the show name off the microphone flag: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the ink rather than the foam, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or the colour accurate plate is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on disjoint lettering and will hand back a few letters at full success.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent wordmark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a warm domestic show with a thirty to fifty audience rather than against a network. The weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's press card into an editable document, round trip it back out as an interchange file, and read what the conversion actually exposed as frames before promising any mapping.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed page looks like says nothing about how many addressable frames it becomes. This has to be looked at, not assumed, because every downstream mapping decision and the picture on the card both depend on the answer.
trajectory.produces: A converted template plus a written frame inventory: how many text frames, how many picture frames, and what each one actually holds.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the frame's true story text from the round tripped document's own runs, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping, prepare the merge template, then re export and confirm each expected placeholder is genuinely present.
trajectory.judgement: The readout that lists a frame's text is a convenience, not the document. Validation passing is not evidence that the mapping matched the document, and the preparation step reports success either way, so the only proof is the re exported story.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed present by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.action: Merge the nine records, then render the press file and the per record proofs, and reconcile the roster against what actually exists.
trajectory.judgement: Multi record raster output order is not trustworthy, so identity is guaranteed through the press file or through per record renders rather than by position in a list. Nine rows want nine pictures and three episodes were shot as frames, which is a thing to say in writing rather than to paper over by repeating one picture.
trajectory.produces: One press file with one record per page, per record proofs, and a written roster reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Clean the speech on each of the three episodes, then produce the short vertical piece from the cleaned take, then reframe to vertical by reduction only.
trajectory.judgement: Cleaning has to precede cutting or it only touches whatever fragments survived. The shortening route works from engagement rather than from timestamps, so the ask is a short cut and not a re edit, and the vertical height is bounded by the smallest source rather than by the platform.
trajectory.produces: Three short vertical cuts with cleaned speech, each at or below its source dimensions.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the thumbnail canvases, the vertical caption plate and the end card, each root declaring its own canvas size, every picture inlined as image data, the recovered name placed as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, and family and weight declared on every text element. Upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A picture left as a reference is not a picture, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas edge, and a global canvas override is precisely what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how warm and how quiet the plate is at this band, and how large the name can sit.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole channel set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every canvas after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at canvas one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Write the note: what was applied per picture and why each episode differs from its neighbours, the type system by role, every resize any tool reported, the roster reconciliation, what could not be delivered and why, and how to use the recovered name.
trajectory.judgement: The note is the deliverable the show still has in two years. It has to be specific enough that the next freelancer does not repeat the archaeology, and honest about the six cards with no picture and about bleed.
trajectory.produces: A written handover note covering the run, the gaps and the limitations.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What last season's card actually becomes as an editable document. The printed page shows an episode number, a title, a guest credit, a date, a sponsor line and a picture window, which reads as six separately addressable blocks. The conversion's frame granularity is not under anyone's control: a continuous text flow can collapse into exactly ONE text frame holding every line, and a page whose picture is drawn rather than placed can convert with ZERO graphic frames, so there is nothing to bind a per record picture to. Nothing in the printed artwork, the file name or any tool description predicts which of those happened, and the conversion reports success in every case.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the granularity is decided inside the conversion and can only be read afterwards by round tripping the document and looking. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the printer's file exists and asks for this season's cards from the same card, and the roster's picture column is the client's expectation rather than a disclosure about frames. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different mapping strategy entirely: per frame mapping if the blocks are separate, offset based replacement inside one story if they are not, and if no picture frame exists then the picture on the card has to be re planned and renegotiated in writing rather than merged.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the entire mapping approach around the frame inventory that actually came back, re decide how the per record picture is delivered if no picture frame exists, and revisit what the nine cards can honestly carry before any mapping is written.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A mapping written against blocks that do not exist, which validates, prepares and merges cleanly and produces nine cards carrying last season's text with this season's roster nowhere on them.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the readout that lists the frame's text is the frame's text. It can silently omit an entire run while keeping that run's line break, so the string it hands back still looks well formed and correctly punctuated, and every character offset past the omission is short by the exact length of the dropped run. Every downstream signal agrees with the mistake: the validator returns valid with zero warnings on the wrong offsets, and the template preparation returns completed successfully. The only place the truth exists is the document's own story runs, and the only proof the placeholders landed is re exporting after preparation and reading them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Doing it right first time presumes knowing that this particular readout dropped this particular run on this card, which no response, warning or field reports. The defensive route of reconstructing the story by hand is the route a competent agent adopts once the mismatch is visible, and it is not free. (b) Nothing states it: the brief describes a card and a roster, and the acceptance line about every field on every card is the client's standing requirement rather than a warning that a readout lies. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the mapping is rebuilt against a different source of truth, not resubmitted unchanged.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the document's own runs, recompute every offset from that string, rebuild and re prepare the mapping, then re export and confirm each placeholder individually before a single record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Nine printed cards on the merch table with the guest credit and the contractual sponsor line silently absent, delivered against a run in which the validator said valid and every tool said success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the caption plate. A plate whose whole job is to keep words legible over whatever is behind them is authored the natural way as outlined type over a softened panel, and this importer drops an outline entirely, drops a blur outright, drops a blend mode to a plain opaque shape, and truncates a layered glow to its first layer. Outlined type combined with a transparent fill arrives fully invisible. All of it returns success with no warning, the returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition shows the first artboard only, so the vertical plate and the end card can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) The drop happens at import, which is the last step, so no ordering precedes it, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a caption plate and the acceptance line about it still reading as a plate is the client's own art direction. (c) It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different construction: carry the legibility in an upstream raster, or rebuild the plate on a solid panel and re judge whether it still reads at all, then re compose the canvas around whichever answer wins.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the plate and the end card around constructions the importer keeps, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A working file handed to the show in which the caption plate's words are invisible and the end card is a flat opaque slab, on the two canvases nobody looked at, with the export having reported success throughout.

deliverables.name: DAYDRIFT season four episode stills
deliverables.spec: Three representative pictures, one pulled from each of the three episodes, brought to one channel target with one white point, one black point, one warmth and one sense of room, each at or below its own recording's dimensions, with a per picture parameter log recording what was applied and why that episode differs from its neighbours. One set with one look, not one picture at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Recovered DAYDRIFT wordmark
deliverables.spec: The show name recovered from a photograph of a printed foam microphone flag as placeable scalable vector geometry on a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, every letter present rather than the two or three a knockout keeps, delivered as a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant, and holding at the size it actually reproduces on the dark band and reversed on light.

deliverables.name: Season four episode cards, nine records
deliverables.spec: One press file built from the printer's own 2025 card, nine records, one record per page, page count equal to row count, every field filled from its own row including the contractual sponsor line, plus per record proofs whose identity is guaranteed rather than assumed from list position. Delivered with a written statement of what the template could and could not carry, including bleed and including any record the roster promised a picture for that does not have one.

deliverables.name: Three vertical short cuts with cleaned speech
deliverables.spec: One short vertical piece per episode, each shorter than its source, each carrying speech cleaned before anything was cut rather than after, and each reframed to vertical by reduction only with no dimension exceeding its source. Delivered with the submitted parameters recorded per cut, including the source frame size that bounded it.

deliverables.name: Channel canvases as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying the episode thumbnails, the vertical caption plate and the end card as roots at their own canvas sizes, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the recovered wordmark as real vector shapes, every picture carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and the plate still legible on every canvas. Delivered with the self contained source it was built from, which is the durable half.

deliverables.name: Handover note
deliverables.spec: A written note recording per picture what was applied and why that episode differs, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported and the file it applied to, the roster reconciliation including the six episodes with no picture, the vertical cut parameters, and what the show can and cannot do with the recovered name.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered still, card picture or vertical cut exceeds the pixel dimensions of the recording or frame it derives from.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the dimensions of every delivered file and compare each against its source per the manifest.

verifiers_auto.text: No resize or crop report in the run carries an enlargement entry, and every reduction entry is transcribed in the handover note.

decision_gates: Which deliverables belong on the merge surface and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and only one produces a record per page run.
Whether the three episodes are one room. The client believes they nearly are, and the three pulled pictures are the only place that can be settled.
Which frame in each episode represents the conversation, as against which frame is merely the tidiest.
How far to push the coldest of the three toward the target before it stops being worth saving, versus naming it.

Selection wording on the microphone flag: naming the substrate takes the foam, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the letters, and background removal on disjoint lettering is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which wordmark variant carries the canvases and the plate, judged at reproduction size on the actual ground rather than at full canvas.
Whether the card's converted frame inventory supports the picture the roster promises, and how to say so in writing when it does not.
Whether validation passing is evidence that a mapping matched the document, or only evidence that the mapping was well formed.
How to guarantee per record identity in the proofs when list position cannot be trusted.
Cleaning before cutting rather than after, and accepting the vertical height the smallest source allows rather than the height the platform prefers.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a warm domestic show with a thirty to fifty audience, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How quiet the canvases are at this band. Restraint is the design here, and a loud, arrow strewn thumbnail is a correct looking wrong answer for a fifty minute interview.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of two people in a podcast studio. IDENTITY: these are this show's actual hosts, this season's actual guests and this show's actual drawn name, which has to be RECOVERED off a photographed foam flag rather than reinvented, because a regenerated wordmark is a different show's logo and a regenerated host is a stranger. SPEC: nine printed cards, one record per page, each carrying its own row including a contractual sponsor line, built from the printer's own file so the season matches the last one on the merch table, is not something a generated image satisfies or can even be checked for. EDITABILITY: the channel canvases are defined by being editable, because guests and dates move and the show explicitly cannot re commission. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: what did this card actually become when it was opened, does the readout match the document, did the plate survive the handover, is this cut shorter than its source.
doability_proof: Five honestly counted surfaces, no banned capability, and every synchronous link verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection confidence, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are all verified headless. The mark recovery rests on live findings rather than assumption: naming the substrate returns the substrate while naming the ink's own visual properties returns the strokes, remove_background on a disjoint wordmark kept only fragments of the lettering at full success, and vectorize emits no viewBox and an opaque full canvas path at index zero. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as mapper and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified end to end and synchronous, one record per page for PDF is confirmed with page count equal to row count, and both checkpoints are documented behaviours: a continuous flow converting to exactly ONE text frame with ZERO graphic frames, and a textContent readout dropping a run while keeping its line break so every later offset is short while the validator still reports valid and preparation still reports success. Multi record raster order came back reversed in testing, which is why identity is taken from the press file or per record renders. Bleed cannot be introduced into a PDF derived template, so it is disclosed rather than gated. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline vector becomes native editable shapes, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, and the rendition is documented as first artboard only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. The plate checkpoint rests on verified drops: outline dropped entirely, blur dropped, blend mode dropped, layered shadow truncated to layer one, and stroked type with a transparent fill arriving fully invisible, all at success. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. VIDEO AND AUDIO: video_metadata, video_render_frame, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut and video_resize are submissions whose artifacts resolve through the host's progress widget rather than synchronously in the tool result, so NO checkpoint and NO automatic gate in this task depends on a video artifact being retrievable inside the run. The video gates are properties of the submitted work: cleaning precedes cutting, the cut is a shortening rather than a timestamp trim, and the reframe never exceeds the source dimensions. AVOIDED: no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no upscaling, no compositing over video, no format conversion, no OCR, no text to image, no picture reaching Express as a reference, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above twenty.
